description: Run KQL/T-SQL/management against an eventhouse cluster. One-shot by default (bounded by --timeout); --follow streams NDJSON for continuous monitoring, always bounded so it terminates.
notes: One-shot query (default) returns the normal {data,count} envelope — a bounded result set. Kusto queries are request/response and always terminate; add --timeout <seconds> (Kusto servertimeout, max 3600) to cap a long-running query. The query runs against the eventhouse's sole KQL database by default; pass --database <name> when the cluster hosts more than one (see 'eventhouse list-databases'). A leading '.' runs a management command (e.g. .create table / .ingest / .show), a leading SELECT runs T-SQL, otherwise KQL.
query_examples: fabio eventhouse query -w <WS> --id <EH> --kql "Logs | where Level == 'Error' | take 100"

follow_mode.description: --follow polls the query every --interval seconds and streams ONE NDJSON object per cycle to stdout, then a final follow_complete summary. It ALWAYS terminates — bounded by --max-duration (default 60s), the global --limit (total rows), or Ctrl-C — so it is safe for an agent/CI caller. Since Kusto has no server-push streaming, 'continuous' is client-side polling. --dedup-column <col> emits only rows whose value in <col> exceeds the max seen so far (incremental tail); without it each cycle re-emits the full result (watch semantics).
follow_mode.command: fabio eventhouse query -w <WS> --id <EH> --kql "Errors | order by ts asc" --follow --interval 2 --max-duration 30 --dedup-column ts
